label: prop:baryon-product-from-alt
title: The baryon integrand $\prod_k dc_k/dz$ is the $\mathrm{Alt}^3$-isotype of the color-tube Jacobian
html:
Let F(z, c) \in R[z, c] be the color-tube cubic (color-tube cubic) with roots c_1(z), c_2(z), c_3(z) over the categorical base ring R. Let \mathrm{S}_3 act on the three color sheets by permutation. The canonical Wedderburn decomposition is

  R[\mathrm{S}_3]
  \;\cong\;
  R \oplus R \oplus R^{2 \times 2}
  \quad
  (\text{trivial} \;\oplus\; \text{sign} \;\oplus\; \text{standard}).

The integrand

  \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}}(z)
  \;:=\;
  \prod_{k=1}^{3} \frac{dc_k}{dz}

is the projection onto the \mathrm{Alt}^3 (sign) isotype of the \mathrm{S}_3-module \bigotimes_{k=1}^3 \,T_{c_k}\mathbf{C} generated by the color-sheet velocities. The sum \sum_k dc_k/dz projects onto the trivial isotype. The sum \sum_{k \neq l} (dc_k/dz)(c_l + z) projects onto the standard isotype.

Here the product \prod_{k=1}^{3} dc_k/dz is the wedge dc_1 \wedge dc_2 \wedge dc_3 evaluated on the diagonal color-sheet frame (see the proof), antisymmetric under sheet exchange — not a symmetric product. This purely algebraic statement holds over R and does not use the archimedean fibre functor \tau \colon R \to \mathbb{R}.

The \mathrm{Alt}^3 isotype is a genuinely non-trivial sign line, not a channel indistinguishable from the trivial one. The monodromy of the color-tube cubic around its discriminant is the full \mathrm{S}_3 — computed exactly over R = \mathbb{Q}[z] and cross-checked at 50 digits (six simple branch points, each a transposition, together generating \mathrm{S}_3; monodromy witness) — so its sign character is surjective onto \{\pm 1\}. Fixing the baryon to this sign isotype therefore fixes the integrand up to a scalar.
